United States Department of the Interior
OFFICE OF THE SECRETARY WASHINGTON, D.C. 20240
In Reply Refer To: ER-74/1369
DEC 31 19/4
Dear Mr. Jones:
This Department has received and reviewed the draft environmental statement for the Ross Ice Shelf Project, U. S. Antarctic Research Program. We find that, for the most part, the document is satisfactory with regard to our areas of expertise and jurisdiction.
Potential adverse environmental impacts related to geologic conditions appear to have been given adequate consideration in the draft statement. We anticipate that the project will have no adverse impact on minerals and will, in fact, increase our knowledge of the mineral potential of that area of the Antarctic.
We agree that the possibility of release of hydrocarbons during drilling into the sea bottom is remote and that planned preventive measures render such a release even less likely. Recent experiences in drilling the sea bottom in the ice-free area of the Ross Sea by the Glomar Challenger could be cited as precedent.
We also agree that the only direct impact likely on fresh-water resources would involve the upper ice itself and that all anticipated effects should be temporary and minimal as far as these resources are concerned.
We wish to note, with reference to page 30, paragraph 2, that the statement that "maximum depth of sediment drilling becomes a function of the drilling rate versus depth of water" might have been intended to read, ". . . function of the drilling rate versus the rate of ice movement."
